properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 13 at 12:09PM AKDT until September 15 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...
Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk: Water levels as
high as 1.0 to 2.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 40 to 45 mph before
winds transition to west Tuesday morning, diminishing impacts.

Toksook Bay and Tununak: West winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts to
45 to 50 mph beginning Tuesday morning. Water levels as high as
0.5 to 1.5 feet above the normal highest tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kwigillingok,
Kongiganak, Kipnuk, Toksook Bay, and Tununak.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Monday to 10 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is potential for coastal erosion due to high
surf. The coastal flood threat is low to medium for
Kwigillingok, Kongiganak, and Kipnuk (30 to 40 percent). The
coastal flood threat is low (10 to 20 percent) for Toksook Bay
and Tununak.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A developing low pressure system will drive
a fetch of strong southwest winds towards the Kuskokwim Delta
Coast early Monday afternoon, which will result in increased
wave activity. Large breaking waves of 3 to 5 feet for the
Kuskokwim Delta coast will continue into Tuesday morning, which
will also coincide with high tide, enhancing coastal impacts.
Southwest winds shut off later Tuesday morning for the Kuskokwim
Delta Coast and attention then shifts to Toksook Bay and Tununak
as west winds take over and the low moves inland. Strong west
winds will bring in higher seas of 1 to 3 feet for Toksook Bay
and Tununak. Conditions are on track to improve as the low moves
farther inland Tuesday night. Additionally, periods of moderate
to heavy rainfall will precede the advisory duration.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect the
coastline in the advisory area, producing rip currents and
localized erosion.


-AM

properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued September 11 at 5:05PM PDT until September 13 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
are possible over the Paradise and Hagen burn scar.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast Oregon, including the following area,
Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon and southeast Washington,
including the following area, Northwest Blue Mountains.

* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Paradise and Hagen burn scar 1 to
1.5 inches is expected during the period of the watch. Residents
near the Paradise and Hagan burn scar should prepare for potential
debris flow. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of
low-lying areas and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the burn scar, which may lead to flash flooding and
debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Meacham, Spout Springs, Tollgate, Bingham Springs, Minam, Ski
Bluewood, Gibbon, Hilgard, Troy, Kamela, Umatilla Reservation and
Kooskooskie.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
